can_execute.quote: Composer spots it in your customer data, then plans and launches personalized campaigns across every channel.
can_execute.note: Confirmed on a second read. The Composer page adds that it 'can create and update campaigns, flows, and other marketing experiences in Klaviyo' and that 'Customer-facing campaigns, flows, and messages require your approval before they're sent or published.' So it acts itself, after approval.

multi_agent.note: The homepage heading 'Your data, intelligence, and AI agents working as one' was re-read: it describes one platform, not agents collaborating with each other. Two named agents exist (Composer, Customer Agent) but no sentence says they work together.

integrations.note: Names readable as text on /integrate, in page order. The page claims '400+ apps'; a logo grid there had no readable names. It also names Snowflake, BigQuery and Azure as export targets, and the Composer FAQ names Asana.

pricing.quote: Up to 250 active profiles and 500 emails per month.
pricing.note: Free plan shown as '$0'. Email plan '$20/month' at the default 500-profile setting of a slider ('Select your number of active profiles'). A limited-time promotion shows the Marketing plan as '$1/month' for the first month (struck-through $25).

hq_location.note: The address is written '125 Summer Street, Floor 6 / Boston, MA 02111'. No country word is printed next to it; 'United States' is derived from the state code and ZIP in that address.

notes: The about page lists offices in eight cities. Plan prices are driven by an interactive profile-count slider, so a plain fetcher may see only the default figures. Expected to be the hardest site in the set for a plain HTTP client (see README); the reading tool itself got full text on all five pages.
